rdc_gateway_problem._note: This is Ian's flagship systems thinking demonstration. It illustrates how he diagnoses invisible scaling problems in distributed IoT systems.
rdc_gateway_problem.context: Inductosense deploys ultrasonic sensors (RDCs — Remote Data Collectors) on industrial pipework to monitor corrosion and wall thickness. Data is collected via wireless gateways and processed in the cloud.

rdc.function: Each sensor port can be scheduled to take ultrasonic thickness readings at a defined interval (e.g. once per minute, once per hour, once per day)
rdc.storage: Stores readings locally until a gateway connects to extract them
rdc.acquisition_time: Each reading takes a finite time to acquire. If scheduled at 1/minute across 8 sensors, the RDC completes a full cycle in ~8 minutes, then immediately starts again

gateway.function: Wirelessly connects to multiple RDCs, extracts stored readings, forwards to cloud
gateway.constraint: Extraction takes time — the gateway must connect to each RDC sequentially, wait for data transfer, then move to the next. This competes with ongoing RDC acquisition.

device_communication_manager.function: Orchestrates all gateways via a task queue system. Works through each gateway in turn, instructing it to collect from its RDCs.
device_communication_manager.constraint: Sequential task processing means that the time to complete a full collection cycle across all gateways and all RDCs grows non-linearly with scale

scaling_problem.description: At small scale (few RDCs, infrequent readings), fixed scheduling works. As scale increases, the interaction between acquisition time, extraction time, gateway capacity, and DCM task queue creates timing collapse that is invisible without visualisation.
scaling_problem.naive_approach: Fixed schedule — 'collect every N minutes' — assumes the system can always keep up. This breaks silently: readings queue up, extraction falls behind acquisition, data gaps appear with no obvious cause.
scaling_problem.what_happens_at_scale: With 95 RDCs per gateway × multiple gateways × 8 sensors each × 1 reading/minute, the total data throughput demand rapidly exceeds what the extraction pipeline can service. The system appears to work but is silently losing data.
scaling_problem.non_obvious_insight: The problem isn't any single component — it's the interaction between all of them. No single engineer 'owns' the bottleneck because it emerges from the system as a whole.
scaling_problem.solution: Dynamic scheduling — the DCM monitors actual queue depth and adjusts extraction priority in real time, rather than assuming a fixed cadence. This requires understanding the whole system, not just individual components.

rdc_gateway_problem.why_it_was_hard_to_see: The business could not comprehend the scale of the problem because there was no visual representation of how the timing interactions worked. A static description or spreadsheet did not convey the emergent complexity. A visual diagram showing how each additional RDC and gateway added to the overall timing load made the problem — and the solution — immediately obvious to non-technical stakeholders.
rdc_gateway_problem.ians_role: Diagnosed the scaling problem, visualised it, and designed the dynamic scheduling architecture that resolved it. Used AI to generate initial visualisations that made the problem comprehensible to the business.
